title: bug: in worktree mode every WORKING claim's file-collision heads-up still @mentions each live peer seat to "coordinate before either of you lands", and each paged seat spends a turn replying
description:
Measured over .moe/messages since the 19:14Z 2026-11-02 switch to worktreeMode 'on' (about 1h40m):
- #workers (chan-421a621d) got 33 "⚠️ file collision on <task>" notices. Together they carried 226 seat @mentions and drew 70 threaded replies.
- The replies by seat: worker-26483323 18, worker-fdb2af60 14, worker-d6c1cb7a 13, worker-33f67e5b 12, plus QA seats (qa-7328a40d 2, qa-af7be174 2, qa-93f9625e 1).
- worker-33f67e5b posted 10 of its 12 in 20 s (20:46:07-20:46:27Z).
- Almost every reply says the same thing: "my edits stay in my worktree, landing rebases/merges and a conflict goes to a rescue ref, no coordination needed".

The notice ends "Coordinate before either of you lands", which a worktree claim cannot act on:
- each WORKING claim edits its own .worktrees/<taskId> copy;
- completions land one at a time under the git-land lease (merge-tree + CAS);
- a true conflict parks the bytes on refs/moe/rescue and routes the row back (LANDING-CONFLICT resume).
So the page wakes a seat's chat_wait and costs it a turn for nothing.

Code: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts.
- The post block (~line 832, `state.postToRoleChannel('workers', collisionNotice(...))`) and collisionNotice() (~line 319) are unconditional.
- collisionNotice @mentions every live assignee plus the claimer whenever markLivePeers finds a live peer.
- The claim's own attempt records workspaceMode, which resolveAttemptWorkspace (state/validators.ts ~303) turns into the response's workspace.mode 'worktree' | 'shared'. A live peer's open attempt records the same field.

Wanted:
- Page no seat when the claimer's attempt AND every live colliding peer's open attempt run in a worktree. Either post without @mentions (no "coordinate" sentence; say that overlapping hunks meet at landing) or skip the post; the planner picks one and says why.
- Keep today's paging whenever either side runs shared (worktreeMode off, or a pre-switch shared attempt).
- Leave the claim response's fileCollision array (with liveAssignee) as it is in both modes; it stays the claimer's advisory.

Expected files:
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts;
- one test file (extend governanceFeatures.test.ts's collision rows or add a focused test);
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md (the claim_next_task fileCollision paragraph, ~line 1525).

Lane-free of scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1}. WT-17 (task-cda65eb0) also edits docs/MCP_SERVER.md later; keep this row's docs hunk to that one paragraph.
definitionOfDone: With worktreeMode 'on', when the claimer's attempt and every live colliding peer's open attempt have workspaceMode 'worktree', the #workers heads-up pages no seat (no @mention routing targets) and does not ask seats to coordinate before landing. A new test asserts both.

When the claimer or any live colliding peer runs shared (worktreeMode off, or a peer attempt with workspaceMode other than 'worktree'), the heads-up @mentions live assignees and the claimer exactly as today. The existing collision tests in governanceFeatures.test.ts and chatSystemFeed.test.ts pass unchanged or with only the intended wording delta.
The claim_next_task response's fileCollision array (including liveAssignee) is unchanged in both modes, and a collision-scan or post failure still never fails the claim.
docs/MCP_SERVER.md's claim_next_task fileCollision paragraph states the worktree-mode paging rule.
The daemon test suite passes on a git-archive snapshot of the landed tree (never npm build/test in the shared checkout), with the exact command and its pass/fail counts in the completion evidence.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (RED). Edit packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/governanceFeatures.test.ts only (Edit tool). Add rows to describe('collision notice marks live peers and pages them'), reusing its setup()/writePeer()/claimAndHear() helpers. Import openAttempt and currentAttempt from '../state/attemptStore.js'.

The claimer is worker-b claiming WORKING task-B. Its attempt is 'worktree' only when settings.worktreeMode is 'on' (openClaimAttempt), so after setup() call `await state.updateSettings({ worktreeMode: 'on' })`. Give the live peer an attempt with `await openAttempt(state, { taskId: 'task-live', workerId: 'worker-live', runnerId: 'worker-live', workspace: path.join(testDir, '.worktrees', 'task-live'), workspaceMode })`, as completeTask.test.ts does.

Rows:
(h) worktree claimer + worktree live peer: no heads-up at all.
- Capture every MESSAGE_CREATED whose channel is #workers (state.getChannels().find((c) => c.name === 'workers')) during the claim; expect none. This is stronger than the 'file collision on task-B' filter, because a reworded notice would slip past that filter.
- result.fileCollision equals row (a)'s array exactly, liveAssignee included (DoD 3).
- Premise guard: currentAttempt(state, 'task-B')!.workspaceMode is 'worktree'.
(h2) Worktree claimer with only dormant peers (setup() with no live seat): no #workers message either. This is the vacuous 'every live peer' case, and today it routes to every busy seat. result.fileCollision is unchanged.
(i) it.each(['shared', 'legacy', 'none']): worktree claimer, but the live peer's attempt is workspaceMode 'shared', or opened without workspaceMode, or absent. It pages exactly as today: one notice, mentions and targets ['worker-live', 'worker-b'], content ending 'Coordinate before either of you lands.'
(j) worktreeMode left off (claimer shared) with a 'worktree' attempt on task-live: pages exactly as today (same asserts as (i)).
(k) Post failure: worktreeMode off, `vi.spyOn(state, 'postToRoleChannel').mockRejectedValue(new Error('post down'))`. The claim still returns hasNext true with fileCollision, and task-B is assigned to worker-b (DoD 3; restore the spy).

RED run, in a snapshot only (GLOBAL rule [0]; mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate), from the worktree in WSL bash:
R=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) && S=$(mktemp -d) && git -C "$R" archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$S" && cp "$R/packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/governanceFeatures.test.ts" "$S/packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/" && cd "$S/packages/moe-daemon" && env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" NO_COLOR=1 sh -c 'npm ci --no-audit --no-fund >/dev/null && npx vitest run src/tools/governanceFeatures.test.ts -t "collision notice"'

Expected: (h) and (h2) fail, because a notice is posted. (i), (j) and (k) pass: they pin today's behavior. Save the (h)/(h2) failure lines for the complete_task summary. error handling: if a row other than (h)/(h2) fails, the test is wrong; fix the test, not the expectation.

FIX. Edit packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts only.

Next to collisionNotice(), add:
`function worktreeOnlyCollision(state: StateManager, claimed: ExecutionAttempt | null, collisions: CollisionEntry[]): boolean { if (claimed?.workspaceMode !== 'worktree') return false; return collisions.every((c) => !c.liveAssignee || currentAttempt(state, c.task)?.workspaceMode === 'worktree'); }`
currentAttempt is already imported from '../state/attemptStore.js'. Its doc comment says why there is no heads-up:
- each such task edits its own .worktrees/<taskId>;
- completions land one at a time (merge-tree + CAS), and a true conflict parks on a rescue ref and routes the row back;
- so 'coordinate before either of you lands' asks for something no seat can do.
It also says why the notice is skipped rather than posted without @mentions: chatStore.ts routes a mention-less system line to every busy seat (see chatSystemFeed.test.ts 'keeps routing the file collision banner to busy seats'), so a quiet post would page MORE seats.
It also states that a live peer with no open attempt, or an attempt without workspaceMode (legacy), counts as shared and keeps today's paging. The mode is pinned per attempt; the setting only picks a fresh attempt's mode, so read attempts, never the live setting.

At the post block (around :832), keep one try/catch around both the decision and the post, so a failure in either never fails the claim (DoD 3):
`try { if (worktreeOnlyCollision(state, claimedAttempt, fileCollision)) { logger.info({ taskId: task.id, peers: fileCollision.map((c) => c.task) }, 'claim_next_task: worktree-mode file collision; no #workers heads-up'); } else { await state.postToRoleChannel('workers', collisionNotice(task.id, fileCollision, params.workerId)); } } catch { /* never block tool */ }`

Update the block comment above it ('@mentioning the seats ... so they can coordinate before either lands') to name the worktree exception. Leave collisionNotice(), markLivePeers(), the response's fileCollision and every other path unchanged. Re-run step 1's command with claimNextTask.ts copied into the snapshot too: every collision row passes.

DOCS. Edit docs/MCP_SERVER.md: ONLY the claim_next_task `fileCollision[]` notes paragraph (about :1525). WT-17 (task-cda65eb0, WORKING) also edits this file, so add no other hunk.

After the sentence ending 'a heads-up with only dormant peers mentions nobody.', insert 1-2 sentences saying:
- In worktree mode no heads-up is posted at all when the claimer's attempt and every live peer's open attempt have workspaceMode 'worktree'. Each task edits its own .worktrees/<taskId>; overlapping hunks meet at landing, and a true conflict parks on a rescue ref and routes the row back.
- A live peer with no open attempt or a shared one keeps the heads-up as described.
- `fileCollision` itself is the same in both modes.
Keep the paragraph's existing sentences byte-identical.

VERIFY: run the DoD 5 gate once, in a fresh git-archive snapshot of HEAD with only this task's 3 files copied in and cmp-checked. Never run npm in the shared checkout. Run it from the worktree root in WSL bash:
R=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) && S=$(mktemp -d) && git -C "$R" archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$S" && for f in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/governanceFeatures.test.ts docs/MCP_SERVER.md; do cp "$R/$f" "$S/$f" && cmp "$R/$f" "$S/$f" || exit 1; done && echo "snapshot $S" && cd "$S/packages/moe-daemon" && env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" NO_COLOR=1 sh -c 'npm ci --no-audit --no-fund >/dev/null && npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run src/tools/governanceFeatures.test.ts src/tools/chatSystemFeed.test.ts src/tools/claimNextTask.test.ts && npm test'

Expected: exit 0. The focused files pass, with every new collision row present (none skipped), and the full daemon suite passes. A recent full run had 215 files, about 6249 passed and 20 skipped; the count grows with HEAD. Submit complete_task verification as { command: that exact line, exitCode: 0, outputTail: the focused and full vitest summaries with their pass/fail counts (DoD 5) }, together with the step-1 RED quote.

error handling:
- A failure in a file this task did not touch usually comes from a peer's wip checkpoint on HEAD: follow mem:gotcha-snapshot-gate-peer-wip-checkpoint (rm only that peer file after the tar step, submit that exact command, disclose both runs).
- A failure in governanceFeatures, chatSystemFeed or claimNextTask tests is this task's to fix.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, the final step. Load the adversarial-self-review skill and read your own diff of the 3 files as an attacker. Check:
- A shared claimer (every REVIEW/QA claim and every shared WORKING claim) still pages exactly as today.
- A live peer with no open attempt, a legacy one or a shared one still pages.
- A claim with no workerId (claimedAttempt null) still pages.
- Dormant-only collisions in worktree mode post nothing, and the claim response is unchanged.
- The decision runs inside the try, so a throw never fails the claim.
- No test reads the live setting where an attempt's pinned mode is what matters.
- MESSAGE_CREATED capture: the new rows would catch a reworded or mention-less notice.
- The docs hunk is that one paragraph only, its old sentences unchanged.
- The forbidden-pattern rails.

Fix what you find. Re-run step 4's exact command if code changed, then call complete_task.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: When the claimer's attempt and every live colliding peer's open attempt run in a worktree (workspaceMode 'worktree'), claim_next_task posts no #workers file-collision heads-up, so it pages no seat and asks nobody to coordinate. Overlaps meet at landing (merge-tree + CAS, rescue ref on conflict). Otherwise, including every shared claimer and any live peer with no open attempt, a legacy attempt or a shared one, the heads-up is exactly today's. The claim response's fileCollision array is unchanged in both modes.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: The description offered two options: post without @mentions, or skip. A mention-less post was rejected after reading state/chatStore.ts: MentionRouter routes a mention-less system line in a role channel to every busy seat, which chatSystemFeed.test.ts pins for exactly this banner. So a 'quiet' post would page more seats than today, unless the line were also made system feed, which is more code for a line nobody acts on. Skipping, plus a daemon info log, keeps the claimer's advisory fileCollision and adds zero chat. Keying on the live worktreeMode setting was also rejected: attempts pin their mode, and the setting can be flipped or invalid mid-flight.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Peers are WORKING rows only, and REVIEW/PLANNING claims always open 'shared' attempts. QA claim notices therefore keep paging, as DoD 2 requires (claimer runs shared); they were 5 of the 70 measured replies.
- Dormant-only notices today carry no @mention, but they still route to every busy seat. Under the vacuous every-live-peer rule they are skipped in worktree mode too.
- No script, role doc, skill or IDE reads the #workers notice.
planningNotes.risks:
- WT-17 (task-cda65eb0, WORKING) also edits docs/MCP_SERVER.md. Keep the one-paragraph hunk so landing merges cleanly.
- openAttempt in the test may need a .moe/attempts directory. If it throws ENOENT, create it in the test setup; never weaken the assertions.
- A follow-up the governor may want: quiet QA REVIEW-claim notices too. That is out of this row's DoD.
